source.name: The Arno with Fishermen
source.description:
In this idyllic scene of fishermen working on the Arno River in Florence at low tide, Stradanus carefully depicted important Florentine monuments such as the Campanile, the Florence Cathedral, and the Palazzo Vecchio. The realistic setting reveals his Netherlandish roots in the close attention to naturalistic and topographical details. The crowded composition and exaggerated, often twisting, movements of the figures reveal the Mannerist influence of Stradanus's years in Florence.   
 Stradanus changed his mind about the compositional details and replaced the lower center of the drawing, inserting more fishermen and a reclining river god in the center foreground. With an urn and a horn of plenty, the river god serves as a personification of the Arno, the river that bisects Florence.   
 Stradanus probably made this sheet as part of a series of hunting and fishing scenes commissioned by Grand Duke Cosimo I de' Medici. The designs, most of which were later engraved, were intended for tapestries to decorate the Medici villa at Poggio a Caiano, but only a few tapestries were ever woven. Artisans later copied this scene in a stucco relief in the courtyard of another Florentine palace.
source.material: Pen and brown ink, brown and blue wash, and white gouache heightening, on gray paper, irregular section cut out and replaced at bottom center by artist

ownerReview.en: Florence’s monuments frame fishermen and an allegorical river god. Stradanus probably designed the scene for a Medici tapestry commission. He cut out and replaced the lower centre of the drawing, adding fishermen and the reclining god.
ownerReview.zh: 佛罗伦萨的古迹环绕着渔民与寓意性的河神。斯特拉达努斯可能为美第奇挂毯委托绘制此图；他曾剪去并替换下方中央部分，增添渔民与斜倚的河神。

source.name: Initial P: Saint Paul; Initial P: A Bishop Giving a Letter to a Messenger
source.description: In the initial P at the top of the page, Paul passes a scroll to a messenger who will convey the author's letter to the Philippians, as a bishop, who stands between them, looks on. The monk writing on a scroll in the initial P at lower left suggests the manuscript's monastic origins--it was probably created in a monastic scriptorium and originally used by a community of monks in Bologna, where it was made.
source.material: Tempera colors, gold leaf, and ink
creditText: Images provided here are believed to be in the public domain and are available under CC0 through Getty’s Open Content Program. Texts provided here are © J. Paul Getty Trust, licensed under CC BY 4.0. Terms of use for the Getty logo can be found here.

ownerReview.en: This medieval page shows Paul passing a letter to a messenger, with a bishop looking on. It depicts the letter to the Philippians, rather than Corinthians, and reveals how a Bolognese monastic community pictured the ancient writer more than twelve centuries later.
ownerReview.zh: 这页中世纪手稿描绘保罗把书信递给信使，旁有主教观看。画中是致腓立比人的书信，而非致哥林多人的书信；它展现逾十二个世纪后，博洛尼亚修道团体如何想象这位古代作者。

ownerReview.en: Gratian’s canon-law compilation, connected with teaching in Bologna, became a university textbook across Europe. This French copy preserves the text, a legal scene and readers’ marginal annotations, showing the working materials of medieval legal study.
ownerReview.zh: 格拉提安的教会法汇编与博洛尼亚教学相关，后来成为欧洲大学课本。这部法国抄本保留正文、法律场景与读者页边批注，呈现中世纪法律学习的实物材料。

source.name: Study for a Statue of Queen Isabella
source.description:
Before an altar with a crown on a large cushion, Queen Isabella the Catholic kneels in silent prayer. She kneels atop an ornate bracket with an empty escutcheon and a large crown in the center, flanked by various emblems and trophies including pomegranates, flags, suits of armor, and two nude men.   
 The study gives enough careful detail to allow a stone carver to accurately reproduce this proposed design for a polychrome marble statue of the Spanish queen. The calibrations, numbered one to six along the right side of the sheet, would have allowed another craftsman to judge the scale of the work. The careful shading down the right edge of the bracket and around the emblems that hang from it suggests that these areas should project further forward than the top portion of the design. The rectangular frame around the queen represents a shallow niche.   
 Pedro de Mena y Medrano produced the design for a statue for the main chapel of the cathedral of Granada. A pendant statue portrays Isabella's husband, Ferdinand II of Aragon, who kneels opposite her. So popular were the two statues that they were copied for another cathedral, in Málaga.
source.material: Pen and gray ink and watercolor over black chalk
creditText: Images provided here are believed to be in the public domain and are available under CC0 through Getty’s Open Content Program. Texts provided here are © J. Paul Getty Trust, licensed under CC BY 4.0. Terms of use for the Getty logo can be found here.

ownerReview.en: Made roughly two centuries after Isabella’s rule, the design pairs her with Ferdinand in Granada Cathedral. Her kneeling pose presents a devout monarch; the scale and shaded bracket guide the sculptor in turning this drawing into a commemorative statue.
ownerReview.zh: 此设计晚于伊莎贝拉统治约两世纪，在格拉纳达主教座堂与斐迪南像成对。跪姿表现虔诚君主，比例尺与饰架阴影则帮助雕刻者把画稿转为纪念雕像。

ownerPixelReview: All four full source images individually viewed. Paul is expressly a later Philippians depiction, illustrating the named writer, not a Corinth scene. The Decretum is a French copy of the canon-law work associated by Getty with Bologna teaching, not a claimed Bologna-owned manuscript. Isabella is later commemoration.
